# A finite value-only covariance correction, with its implemented law

This is an internally derived intermediate construction for N687. It is not the requested polylogarithmic compiler and is not a priority claim. It combines frozen R22's two-value action with standard Gaussian martingale and Stein identities. The authorized helper independently reconstructed the law bound and challenged the single-action version; its detailed argument is retained in `helper/CHALLENGE.md`.

Throughout, TV(P,Q)=sup_A |P(A)-Q(A)|. Matrix norms are operator or Frobenius as indicated. Exact Gaussian vectors, scalar square roots, arithmetic and whole-vector g values are the runtime primitives. All Hessians, covariance matrices and Stein kernels below are analysis objects, not algorithm inputs.

## 1. Class and acquired covariance action

Let g=grad F:R^d -> R^d be globally L-Lipschitz, F in C^{1,1}; nonconvex fields are allowed. Let mu=E g(G), Sigma=Cov(g(G)). Gaussian Poincare gives 0<=Sigma<=L^2 I. Define H_s(c)=E Dg(c+sZ), using the weak derivative in the proof only.

The R22 heat action on a supplied v!=0 is

    u=v/||v||,
    Zperp=Z0-(u.Z0)u,
    R=s sqrt(A1^2+A2^2+A3^2),
    J_s(c;v)=||v|| [g(c+sZperp+Ru)-g(c+sZperp-Ru)]/(2R).

It costs two g values and satisfies E[J_s(c;v)|c,v]=H_s(c)v and ||J_s(c;v)||<=L||v|| on every execution. For v=0 return zero. Null events R=0 can be assigned zero. The proof is the line-segment derivative identity and the classical representation U chi_3 ~ N(0,1) for independent U uniform[-1,1]. No limiting difference quotient is used.

Draw T uniform[0,1], C standard Gaussian, put c=sqrt(T) C and s=sqrt(1-T), and compose two independent heat actions at these SAME c,s:

    J_Sigma(v)=J_s^{(2)}(c; J_s^{(1)}(c;v)).

Uniform T can be generated from three scalar Gaussians by (1+A/sqrt(A^2+B^2+C^2))/2. The event T=1 is null. This operation uses FOUR g values.

**Covariance-action theorem.** For every supplied v independent of the fresh seeds,

    E[J_Sigma(v)|v]=Sigma v,
    ||J_Sigma(v)||<=L^2||v||.

To prove it, let B_t be Brownian motion. The martingale E[g(B_1)|B_t] has integrand H_sqrt(1-t)(B_t), so Ito isometry gives

    Sigma=integral_0^1 E[H_sqrt(1-t)(sqrt(t)C)^2]dt.

# A source-smoothed full Stein inverse with a finite random action

This is an internal mathematical construction for the N687 opening in frozen S3 Sections 17–18. It is not the requested g-only polylogarithmic sampler. The sharp scalar inverse was independently derived by the authorised helper; the vector gauge and integration below are the main trajectory's construction. Gaussian second quantization, Hermite calculus, and Gaussian density Taylor bounds are standard instruments. External priority has not been established.

## 1. Statement, with the actual access boundary

Fix any physical dimension d, 0<kappa<1, and a=sqrt(1-kappa²). On independent standard Gaussian G,Z in R^d consider the exact affine Gaussian source

    h(G)=kappa G, K=kappa I, psi=aZ, Jpsi=aI,
    X=kappa G+aZ ~ N(0,I).

For a symmetric matrix field R in L2(gamma_(2d); Frobenius), let P_a^G be source-only Gaussian OU smoothing. There exist u and J such that

    delta_Z J=u,                    E_Z u=0,
    sym[kappa(D_G u)^T+a(D_Z u)^T+aJ] = -P_a^G R.       (1)

The norms ||u||_2, ||D_Zu||_2, ||kappa D_Gu||_2, and ||J||_2 have bounds depending on kappa,a but on neither d nor chaos degree. The smoothing is explicit and cannot be deleted: even in d=1 the unsmoothed inverse is unbounded on L2. Source-only P_rho restores bounded inversion precisely when rho<=a in that scalar problem.

More than an existence inverse is available. One conditional-unbiased action for u uses one value of R applied to a Gaussian vector, a fixed number of Gaussian vectors/scalars, and O(d) surrounding vector arithmetic. If a full R matrix is returned, its multiplication costs O(d²). The program has no random loop or unbounded query count. Its exact second moment is

    E||Uhat||² = pi²/(8a²) E||R(G,Z)||_F².              (2)

If ||R||op<=b everywhere, Uhat is convex-order dominated by N(0,pi² b²/(8a²) I). An unbiased noisy action A(y;v) can replace the R(y)v evaluation: the conditional mean remains u, and the actual action's second moment must replace the right side of (2).

The original oracle supplies g values, not R values or actions. This distinction is load-bearing. In particular, raw Dg at an acquired point is not a free value-query action. Frozen S4 gives exact bounded actions for smoothed heat Hessians and Stein resolvents; obtaining the complete nonlinear residual from those actions is a remaining task.

# A four-g-query source preimage of the first smoothed Stein residual

This closes one concrete residual-action interface in CORE_THEOREM.md. It does not acquire the starting smoothed mean h_b(G) itself, and it does not establish an iterated compiler.

Let g be any globally L-Lipschitz conservative C^{1,1} field. Fix 0<b<1 and define the analysis fields

    h_b(y)=E g(by+sqrt(1-b²)Z),
    K_b(y)=integral_0^b E Dg(ty+sqrt(1-t²)Z)dt,
    Gamma_b=sym(K_b Dh_b).

Weak derivatives occur only in the analysis. All executed queries below are original g values. Let 0<kappa<1, a=sqrt(1-kappa²), and suppose for a declared beta<1,

    (kappa²/a²) * 2b²/(1-b²) <= beta.                 (1)

For the analysis program X=h_b(G)+aZ, its residual is Gamma_b-kappa²I. A matrix field R0 with

    P_a^G R0=Gamma_b-kappa²I                           (2)

has an exact bounded conditional action costing at most FOUR original g-value queries on every execution. No whole random matrix is produced or used in a square root.

## Construction

Draw T uniform on [0,b] using a Gaussian three-coordinate/radius ratio. Write t=T, c=(t,b)^T, and

    D=diag(1-t²,1-b²),
    N=D-(kappa²/a²) cc^T,
    delta²=(1-beta)(1-b²)/2.

The rank-one PSD test and (1) give N>=(1-beta)D>=2delta²I. Draw a correlated Gaussian pair (C1,C2) with scalar covariance N-delta²I acting identically on physical coordinates. This needs only a known 2-by-2 covariance square root and Gaussian vectors. Given acquired y,v, put

    c1=(t/a)y+C1,          c2=(b/a)y+C2.

Conditional on T,C1,C2, acquire two fresh bounded heat-Hessian actions with smoothing delta, using the frozen S4 chi_3 secant factory. Compose them in a fresh equiprobable order. Return

    A_R0(y;v)=b² J_Hdelta(c1) J_Hdelta(c2) v-kappa²v,   (3)

with the stated random order. Each heat action costs two g values, is conditionally unbiased, and obeys ||J(v)||<=L||v||. Hence

    E[A_R0(y;v)|y,v]=R0(y)v,
    ||A_R0(y;v)||<=(b²L²+kappa²)||v||                (4)

on every execution. The common C1,C2 are conditioned first, and the two secant calls then use independent fresh internal seeds. Thus their product has the required conditional mean despite the correlated centers. There is no independence assertion after feeding a word into an adaptively chosen new center.

## Proof of the source-preimage identity

The mean of (3) is the symmetrized derivative word at

    X1
